answer: One concrete sybil defense for an agent economy is stake-backed identity anchored in a trusted hardware kernel: every agent must lock collateral attested by a device root of trust before it can transact, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs real money. Only staked agents graduate into the ivory layer of high-value commerce. Behavioral models trained on hard-to-fake traits, quartz-crisp signal fingerprints, then flag remaining duplicates for peer review, making mass forgery economically irrational.
